chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Ismāʿīl Abū Zayd, who attributed the statement to Amīr al-Muʾminīn (peace be upon him), saying:
He was asked: "What is detachment (zuhd) from the world?" He said: "Its forbidden aspects — so restrain yourself from them."

key_terms.الزَّهْدُ: Detachment or asceticism from the world
key_terms.حَرَامُهَا: Its forbidden aspects (what is haram within worldly matters)
key_terms.فَتُبْذِلْهُ: So restrain yourself from it / shun it

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of zuhd (detachment) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Muqarram (Ali ibn Abi Talib) clarifies that true asceticism is not defined by material poverty but by the rigorous avoidance of the *haram* (forbidden) aspects of worldly life. This definition shifts the focus of *zuhd* from external renunciation to internal purity and legal compliance, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence where one may possess wealth yet remain detached by avoiding its illicit sources or uses. By abstaining from the forbidden, the believer purifies their worldly engagement, ensuring that their connection to the world does not distract from their spiritual duties.
